description: Direct check of C-startup-recovery-newest: create two retained snapshots in a real FileSnapshotStore whose (term, index) positions are inversely ordered (term 9 index 50, then term 4 index 80), then start a real Raft on an empty log and stable store so recovery must come from a snapshot, and compare the applied index it adopts with the highest index the store holds. The oracle is that startup recovery adopts the most advanced retained snapshot (newest_adopted == true); identity is the node label used on both events.

harness.description: In-package Go test that seeds two real snapshots through FileSnapshotStore.Create/Write/Close in inverse (term, index) order, lists them, then constructs Raft with skipStartup and an empty log, and reports the applied index, the adopted snapshot index and the highest retained index.
semantic_changes: skipStartup is set so NewRaft performs validation, term/log reads and the snapshot restore but does not start the background goroutines; the restore path under test is unchanged.
The FSM is a no-op stub, so the restored contents are irrelevant and only raft's own recovery bookkeeping is observed.
The snapshots use an empty Configuration and a real in-memory transport only to satisfy the Create signature.

legality.derivation: NewRaft restores a snapshot whenever the store holds one, and restoreSnapshot tries the listed snapshots in order and keeps the first that loads, so an empty log and stable store make the adopted snapshot the sole source of the applied baseline. FileSnapshotStore.Create accepts any index/term pair, so the inversely ordered retention is a legal store state, and the interface's ordering sentence is what the recovery is entitled to rely on.
legality.applicability: The node starts with an empty log and stable store and a store retaining two snapshots whose terms and indexes are ordered in opposite directions; the restore path is the real one. The proposition is local to this node's recovery.
unresolved: Whether a running node produces inversely ordered retained snapshots.
alternatives: With contract-conformant ordering the recovery would load the highest-index snapshot first, so the observed choice is attributable to the order rather than to the loader.

grounding.derivation: The applied index adopted at startup is the node's recovery position, and the highest retained index is what the store holds, so comparing them tests whether recovery selected the most advanced state the interface promises to list first.
grounding.applicability: Admitted for the node that prepared and then recovered from the retained pair, correlated by the shared node label.
alternatives: A failure to load the higher-index snapshot would be a different cause; the harness uses identical, readable snapshots so only the order differs.

observable_properties.description: Startup recovery must adopt the retained snapshot with the highest applied index; the compared field is the adopted applied index checked against the highest index the store holds.

uncertainties: The check constructs the inversely ordered retention directly; it does not establish that a running node produces it, nor the later consequence of a configuration-scan panic on a hole.
Only the in-repository FileSnapshotStore is exercised.
